title: The Broken Bridge

beats.narrativeText: One of the station's access bridges has partially collapsed — and on the other side of the gap is a storage facility nobody has been able to reach in years.

The storage facility is believed to hold more of the expedition's records, but the bridge itself is beyond a simple repair. Whatever gets the learner across, it won't be fixing what was already there.
The learner works out exactly what the bridge needs to support and what's actually available to build it from, then plans a lightweight design of their own.
Before any building starts, Atlas makes one thing clear: Explorer Academy cares far more about a design that gets better through testing than one that happens to be perfect on the first try.
The learner must build an actual prototype bridge — one that has to hold a specified load, using only the limited materials on hand.
The first attempt doesn't hold. Testing what failed and adjusting the design, the learner gets a second attempt to actually work — and that difference is the whole point.
The learner records exactly what changed between the first attempt and the final one, and reflects on why that specific change mattered.

The bridge holds. For the first time, the learner has built something that stood between them and the answer — and won. The storage facility is open, and whatever the expedition left inside it is finally within reach.

activities.title: Analyse the Engineering Problem
activities.storyContext: A partially collapsed bridge stands between the learner and a storage facility believed to hold more of the expedition's records.
activities.instructions: Work out exactly what the bridge needs to support, and take stock of what materials are actually available to build it.
activities.output: Notes describing the engineering problem to solve.

activities.title: Plan a Bridge Design
activities.storyContext: A good design starts with a clear plan — building first and figuring it out as you go tends to waste your best materials.
activities.instructions: Sketch and plan a lightweight bridge design capable of supporting the specified load, before you build anything.

activities.title: Build a Prototype
activities.storyContext: Atlas is clear that nobody expects this to work perfectly on the first try — Explorer Academy cares about what you do next if it doesn't.
activities.instructions: Build a simple prototype of your bridge design using the available materials.

activities.title: Test and Refine
activities.storyContext: The first prototype rarely works perfectly the first time.
activities.instructions: Test your prototype against the specified load, then refine the design to improve it.
activities.output: A refined bridge prototype and notes on what changed.

activities.title: Record Improvements
activities.storyContext: Explorer Academy cares about understanding why a design improved, not just being able to say that it did.
activities.instructions: Record what you changed between your first and final design, and explain specifically why each change helped it hold more weight.
activities.output: A written record of design improvements.

activities.title: Compare Bridge Structures
activities.storyContext: Different bridge structures are stronger in different ways.
activities.instructions: Compare a few different bridge structures and explain why some are stronger than others.
activities.output: A short explanation comparing bridge structures.

activities.title: How Engineers Choose Bridge Designs
activities.storyContext: Real engineers choose different bridge designs for different environments.
activities.instructions: Find out how engineers choose bridge designs for different environments.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What did you change between your first and final bridge design, and why?

discussionPoints: What was the biggest weakness in your first design?
How did testing help you improve the bridge?
parentGuide.preparation: Simple building materials such as card, straws, tape or craft sticks are useful for the prototype.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for evidence of testing and refinement rather than a single first attempt, and a clear explanation of what was improved.

completionCriteria: A bridge prototype built, tested, refined, and improvements recorded.
